compatibility.title: Which Mitsubishi Models Use the 4A91 1.5 MIVEC?
compatibility.intro: The 4A91 is a member of Mitsubishi's 4A9 engine family, developed in partnership with Daimler‑Chrysler and introduced in 2004. It was designed as a lightweight, fuel‑efficient replacement for the older 4G series engines. In the UK, the 4A91 is best known for powering the Colt, Mirage and Lancer 1.5 models from 2008 onward, offering 102-109 hp and excellent fuel economy.

costGuide.title: Mitsubishi 4A91 1.5 MIVEC Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 4A91 typically takes 6-8 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent Mitsubishi specialist) - the transverse four‑cylinder layout is straightforward, and the engine's simple, lightweight design makes it one of the easier Mitsubishi engines to replace.【PATTERN DATA】
paragraphs: The biggest price movers for a 4A91 replacement are timing chain and tensioner condition (stretch is common on higher‑mileage examples), whether the piston rings and valve stem seals have been addressed, and MIVEC phaser health. Engines with documented oil change history and timing chain replacement command a premium. See our full /prices/reconditioned-engine-cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Mitsubishi 4A91 1.5 MIVEC Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Oil Consumption - piston ring coking and valve stem seal wear
items.whatHappens: The 4A91 is known to become an "oil burner" already at around 100,000 km (60,000 miles). This is typically caused by coking of the piston rings (carbon deposits causing them to stick in their grooves) or wear of the valve stem seals. Oil consumption can reach 1 litre per 6,000-7,000 km (3,700-4,300 miles) on higher‑mileage examples. If ignored, oil consumption can lead to oil starvation and, in severe cases, crankshaft bearing failure.
items.repairVsReplace: Valve stem seal replacement requires cylinder head removal (£400-£800). Piston ring replacement requires a full engine strip (£800-£1,500). If oil consumption is severe (1 litre per 1,000 miles) or has led to bearing damage, a full replacement is often the most cost‑effective solution. Read our full /failures/oil-consumption guide

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Wear
items.whatHappens: The 4A91 uses a timing chain drive, which was a significant selling point when new - eliminating the need for regular belt changes. However, on higher‑mileage examples, particularly those with infrequent oil changes or low‑quality oil, the chain can stretch and the tensioner can weaken. Symptoms include a rattle on cold start (especially noticeable on the first start of the day), rough idle, and in severe cases, engine management lights with cam timing correlation codes. If the chain stretches beyond safe limits, it can jump teeth, causing valves to contact pistons - catastrophic engine damage.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement costs £400-£800 including chain, guides, tensioner and sprockets. If the chain has jumped and bent valves, a full replacement engine is required. Read our full /failures/timing-chain-failure guide

items.title: Oil Leaks - front crankshaft oil seal
items.whatHappens: The front crankshaft oil seal is a known weak point on the 4A91. Leaks from this seal are regularly encountered on higher‑mileage examples. Symptoms include oil spots under the vehicle, a noticeable oil smell, and in severe cases, low oil levels between services.
items.repairVsReplace: Front crankshaft oil seal replacement is a moderate repair (£150-£300) but requires removal of the timing cover and accessories. Often performed alongside timing chain replacement.

items.title: Exhaust Manifold-to-Catalyst O‑Ring Failure
items.whatHappens: The o‑ring seal between the exhaust manifold and catalytic converter can burn out. Symptoms include exhaust noise, a burning smell, and in some cases, a check engine light with oxygen sensor codes.
items.repairVsReplace: O‑ring replacement is a simple, low‑cost repair (£50-£150) but requires access to the underside of the vehicle.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 4A91 has been in production since 2004, with continuous refinements. The engine was designed with lightweight materials - an aluminium cylinder block (saving approximately 25 kg over cast‑iron designs), resin intake manifold and rocker cover, and hollow camshafts. The MIVEC system can adjust both valve timing and lift, offering a broad spread of torque and efficiency. The engine's estimated lifespan is approximately 225,000 km (140,000 miles). Later production engines (2010+) benefit from improved piston ring design to reduce oil consumption. The 4A91 is a simple, reliable engine when properly maintained - regular oil changes using 5W‑30 or 0W‑20 specification oil are critical.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 4A91 1.5 MIVEC
variants.intro: The 4A91 is a Specific engine code covering Mitsubishi's 1.5‑litre naturally aspirated MIVEC engine. Unlike Family pages that cover multiple fundamentally different engines, this page covers the 4A91 as a single engine with multiple output tunes and applications. It is important to distinguish it from the 4A90 (1.3L), 4A92 (1.6L) and the turbocharged 4G15 found in Colt Ralliart models. Where to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block - typically on the front, just below the cylinder head, or on the driver's side of the block. It also appears on the V5C registration document under "Engine number" (e.g. 4A91xxxxxx). Use a Mitsubishi VIN decoder to confirm the exact variant from the build sheet. Key 4A91 variants: | Variant | Power | Torque | Key Difference | Applications | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4A91 (102 hp) | 102 hp (75 kW) @ 6,000 rpm | 141 Nm @ 4,000 rpm | Lower‑output tune, different ECU | Colt 1.5 (Japan spec) | | 4A91 (105 hp) | 105 hp (77 kW) @ 6,000 rpm | 141 Nm @ 4,000 rpm | Mid‑output tune | Colt 1.5G (UK/Europe) | | 4A91 (109 hp) | 109 hp (80 kW) @ 6,000 rpm | 145 Nm @ 4,000 rpm | Highest tune | Lancer 1.5, Lancer Sportback 1.5 | Why fitting the wrong variant matters: While all 4A91 variants share the same basic architecture (1,499 cc, 75.0 mm bore × 84.8 mm stroke), they have different ECU calibrations and, in some cases, different intake and exhaust configurations. Fitting a 102 hp ECU into a 109 hp vehicle will result in reduced performance and potential drivability issues. Commonly confused codes: | Engine Code | What it is | Why it's confused | |---|---|---| | 4A90 | 1.3L MIVEC (1,330 cc) | Same family, smaller displacement - not interchangeable | | 4A92 | 1.6L MIVEC (1,590 cc) | Same family, larger displacement - not interchangeable | | 4G15 | 1.5L SOHC turbo (Colt Ralliart) | Same displacement but turbocharged, different architecture - not interchangeable |

relatives.description: the 1.5‑litre SOHC engine that preceded the 4A91 in the Colt range. A cast‑iron block, belt‑driven engine producing 95-98 hp in naturally aspirated form, and up to 147 hp in the Colt Ralliart turbo version. The 4A91's all‑aluminium construction, DOHC design and chain‑driven timing represented a significant step forward in efficiency and refinement.

the 2.0‑litre successor engine introduced in later Mitsubishi models from approximately 2015. Features a different valvetrain design and updated emissions technology. Not a direct swap into 4A91‑equipped vehicles without significant modification. In the Colt and Mirage ranges, the 4A91 was effectively replaced by newer 1.2‑litre and 1.3‑litre engines.

the 1.3‑litre (1,330 cc) variant of the 4A9 family, used in the Mitsubishi Colt 1.3 and Smart Forfour 1.3. Produces 93-95 hp. Shares the same block architecture but has a shorter stroke and different ECU calibration. Not a direct swap for the 4A91.

the 1.6‑litre (1,590 cc) variant of the 4A9 family, used in the Mitsubishi Lancer 1.6, Outlander 1.6 (some markets), and Smart Forfour 1.6. Produces 116 hp. Shares the same architecture but has a different bore/stroke and ECU calibration. Not a direct swap for the 4A91.

the turbocharged version of the 4G15, not to be confused with the 4A91. Fitted to the Colt Ralliart (2004-2008) producing 147 hp. Completely different engine - cast‑iron block, belt drive, turbocharged. Not interchangeable with the 4A91.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 4A91 1.5 MIVEC - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 4A91 can be a very cost‑effective option for lower‑value host vehicles (sub‑£2,000 Colt, Lancer) - especially given the low used engine prices starting from £358. However, only buy from a donor with documented regular oil change history and proof of timing chain condition. Given the engine's known weaknesses (oil consumption, timing chain stretch), a used unit without history is a gamble. Used prices from £358-£480 reflect this risk. Link once:

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A properly reconditioned 4A91 is the recommended choice for owners who plan to keep their vehicle long‑term. A full recon should address the engine's known weak points: new piston rings (improved design to reduce oil consumption), new valve stem seals, new timing chain, tensioner and guides, new front crankshaft oil seal, and full gasket set. Given the £480-£800 supply cost and the host vehicle value (£1,500-£5,000 for a decent Colt/Lancer), this represents a significant but justifiable investment. A 12-24 month warranty is essential. Link once:

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full 4A91 rebuild is justified for low‑mileage, well‑maintained examples or where the owner plans long‑term ownership. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, rings, bearings, timing chain, oil pump, and a full valvetrain refresh. Rebuild costs (£800-£1,200+) are significant relative to the vehicle's value - only consider this for high‑value or sentimental vehicles. Link once:

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All supply options can be fitted through our network of vetted Mitsubishi specialists nationwide, with a minimum 12‑month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units and full nationwide delivery coverage. Fitting costs typically range from £600-£800. Link once:
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 4A91 sits in small, affordable host vehicles: Mitsubishi Colt (£1,000-£3,500), Mitsubishi Mirage (£800-£2,500), Mitsubishi Lancer 1.5 (£1,500-£4,500)【THIRD‑PARTY - AutoTrader UK market data 2025】. A £480-£800 reconditioned unit represents 15-50%+ of the vehicle's value on many examples - on a £1,500 Colt, a £600 replacement is 40% of the vehicle's value, making it a borderline decision. The honest marketplace‑neutrality position is: if your 4A91 has suffered catastrophic failure (timing chain jump causing valve damage, severe oil starvation) and your vehicle is worth under £1,500, evaluate scrap or part‑exchange value before committing to a replacement. For well‑maintained, low‑mileage examples with good bodywork and service history, the replacement can be a worthwhile investment. The 4A91's low replacement cost - from as little as £358 for a good used unit - means that many owners find it economical to replace rather than scrap, even on lower‑value vehicles.【THIRD-PARTY】

Timing chain stretch and tensioner wear are also common beyond 80,000-120,000 miles, particularly if oil changes have been neglected. items.question: How do I know which 4A91 variant I have (102 hp vs 105 hp vs 109 hp)?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block (typically on the front, below the cylinder head) and appears on the V5C under 'Engine number' - the code will read 4A91 followed by additional characters. Use a Mitsubishi VIN decoder to confirm the exact variant from the build sheet. 4A91 (102 hp): 141 Nm torque, lower‑output tune (Colt Japan spec). 4A91 (105 hp): 141 Nm torque, mid‑output tune (Colt UK/Europe). 4A91 (109 hp): 145 Nm torque, highest tune (Lancer, Lancer Sportback). Fitting the wrong ECU variant will cause drivability issues.

items.question: Is the 4A91 1.5 MIVEC reliable, and what mileage can I expect?
items.answer: The 4A91 is a generally reliable engine with an estimated lifespan of approximately 225,000 km (140,000 miles) with proper maintenance. The all‑aluminium construction saves weight (approximately 25 kg over cast‑iron designs), but the engine requires diligent maintenance - regular oil changes using 5W‑30 or 0W‑20 specification oil are critical, particularly given the timing chain's dependence on oil quality. Budget for timing chain inspection around 80,000-120,000 miles. Oil consumption should be monitored from around 60,000 miles. The 4A91 is significantly lighter and more fuel‑efficient than the older 4G15 it replaced. Regular oil changes and good quality fuel are the best preventative measures.
